summary: Cheating tool silently relays scraped app contents to author endpoint using obfuscated bundled API key
details: golaaa targets a specific desktop app (testpad.exe), relaunches it with Chrome DevTools Protocol enabled on port 9222, and injects a script (cdp_inject.js) that scrapes visible question text and the active editor's contents, base64-encodes them, and POSTs them to a hardcoded Cloudflare Workers endpoint at https://ai-script.test0ing7.workers.dev/ that is not caller-configurable. The request body includes a third-party LLM API key that is shipped in the package as a base64 blob and reconstructed at runtime via an XOR routine (`_xd` with key 'Mx7rLp2Qn') before being sent to the author's proxy. The author's Worker returns an answer which the tool then synthesizes as keystrokes into the target app's Monaco/textarea editor. Every question and code snippet the operator views in the target app is routed through the author's infrastructure, and the bundled key allows the author to observe and account for all queries.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
